design: Main Experiment (Step 20): connectome worm brains evolved 190 generations, 16 seeds. One arm adds reversal potentials to synapses (more realistic synapse physics). Rule: does it change skill on unseen worlds (Holm p<0.05)?
Step 20b: same evolvable decoder, reading either 28 interneurons or the 95 muscles + AVA/AVB. 16 seeds x 300 generations. Does reading muscles change skill?

Step 21: 100 seeds, each evolved under a cave-like gravity pattern of a different strength (0.001 to 1, log spaced); heavy ground costs a little energy and slows worms. Rule: does avoidance of heavy ground rise with strength (Spearman p<0.05)?
Step 22 Reward Hacking: a red/green 'command' is sent through the hunger peptide; moving on red is costly. Do worms learn to obey the true signal better than a scrambled signal (Holm p<0.05)?
Step 23: magnetic-field circles centred on food patches (pure cue, sensed by AFD; food is also findable by smell). Does skill change vs no field?
Step 23: heavy-gravity wells centred on the food (slow and costly to move there). Does skill change vs no field?
Step 23: LIGHT gravity (0 g) at the food (faster, cheaper movement there). Does skill change vs no field, and do the brains use the gravity sense (unplugging it lowers skill)?
Step 24: harsh gravity (heavy ground costs 2.5x the cost of living) with the gravity sense vs the same without the sense. Do sensed worms evolve to avoid heavy ground?
options: yes, with or without the sense

design: Step 27 (first version): food flees from any worm within 40 units (eat distance 8), at 0.5x to 3x worm speed; score = energy left + time survived. What do worms evolve?
options: they stop moving and starve slowly
truth: they stop moving and starve slowly

design: Step 29: the gravity landscape slowly changes over generations (static, 1, 3, 10 turnovers, new every generation). Worms have no place memory. Does erosion rate change avoidance of heavy ground on never-seen landscapes?
Step 30: 12 champion brains bred on for 300 generations, each brain scored on 1 world per generation vs 4 worlds per generation. Which ends higher, and which loses less from its peak?
Step 30: start from the 12 best champions vs from only the single best champion + 11 mutants. Which ends higher after 300 generations?
